name: Oscilloscope
description: A scope trace opened out into depth: the live waveform at the front and forty earlier ones still standing behind it, receding, rising and twisting away over a flowing grid floor. The waveform is resynthesised from the six band followers rather than stored, which is what makes the depth possible — the trace as it stood a second ago can simply be evaluated. Real perspective, computed in closed form rather than marched.

layers.description: Traces standing behind the live one. This is the main cost: each layer is six sines for any pixel it can reach, and none for the rest.

persist.description: How far back in time each layer sits. 0 stacks identical traces and gives a smooth extruded ribbon; high values make each layer its own waveform and the stack breaks up into weather.

twist.description: Rotation added per layer about the view axis, and the camera roll that goes with it. This is what turns a flat stack into a corkscrew.

speed.description: How fast the partials drift past each other.

amp.description: Vertical gain. Past about 2 the front trace fills the frame and the stack behind it stops reading as depth.

beam.description: Beam width, in pixels, so it holds at any render resolution. Layers thin out with distance whatever this is set to.

tint.description: Pulls the P31 green toward the project palette. The far end of the stack goes to the palette regardless, so depth reads as colour as well as as size.
